title: Improve color coding for vacant/occupied beds and status labels
description: Current vacant/occupied indicators and status badges (invoice Unpaid/Partial/Paid, tenant Active/Vacated, etc.) use similar-looking neutral colors that are hard to tell apart at a glance. Adopt a standard RAG (Red/Amber/Green) -style status-color system: Red for the bad/urgent state (Occupied-overdue, Unpaid), Amber for in-between (Partial), Green for the good state (Vacant/available, Paid, Active) - a convention wardens and staff will already recognize from outside the app, rather than an invented color language. This is a prerequisite for LODGY-32 (dark mode) - land the token system here first so dark mode adjusts these same tokens rather than the two being built independently and drifting.
acceptanceCriteria: A single RAG-based status-color token set is defined once and consumed everywhere, not per-screen ad hoc colors
Vacant vs Occupied beds use the RAG green/red pair consistently across BedGridScreen and VacantViewScreen
Invoice status badges (Unpaid=red/Partial=amber/Paid=green) and tenant status badges (Active=green/Vacated=neutral) follow the same token set app-wide
Color choices remain distinguishable for common color-vision deficiencies (not color-alone - pair with icon/label, see LODGY-62)
LODGY-32 (dark mode) consumes and adjusts these same tokens rather than defining its own

history.note: Added from the v2 feedback session (warden interviews after the v1 field test) and from buried enhancement/limitation notes surfaced while re-reading the full v1 board history.

Resolved the color-system ambiguity: use standard RAG (Red/Amber/Green) status coding rather than inventing a bespoke palette. Also made the LODGY-32 sequencing explicit (this lands first, dark mode consumes its tokens) instead of leaving it as two independent tickets that could drift.

Starting - defining one RAG token set (ui/theme/StatusColors.kt) provided through the theme, a StatusLevel mapping for BedStatus/InvoiceStatus/TenantStatus, and a shared StatusBadge so no screen picks its own colour. Building the tokens as a theme-provided value specifically so LODGY-32 can swap the dark variant without touching call sites.

Built the RAG token set. ui/theme/StatusColors.kt defines StatusLevel (GOOD/WARN/BAD plus NEUTRAL for a state that is neither, i.e. a vacated tenant), StatusPalette (accent + container + onContainer) and Light/DarkStatusColors, handed down through LodgyTheme via LocalStatusColors so LODGY-32 flips the whole app by swapping one value rather than editing call sites. ui/common/StatusBadge.kt holds the single StatusLevel mapping for BedStatus/InvoiceStatus/TenantStatus plus the one StatusBadge composable every screen now draws. Consumers converted: BedGridScreen tiles (green vacant / red occupied instead of primaryContainer-vs-surface), VacantViewScreen rows, InvoiceListScreen's StatusChip (was an untinted SuggestionChip), TenantDirectoryScreen rows and TenantProfileScreen. Green is pulled toward teal and amber toward orange to stay separable under red-green CVD, and every badge still carries its text label - colour is never the only cue (LODGY-62 adds the icon on top of these same tokens). New StatusLevelTest covers the mappings and that each level resolves to a distinct palette in both schemes. testDebugUnitTest green.

PASS on emulator (Pixel-class 1080x2400 @420dpi). AC1: single RAG token set in ui/theme/StatusColors.kt (StatusLevel GOOD/WARN/BAD/NEUTRAL + StatusPalette), exposed via LocalStatusColors and consumed through ui/common/StatusTokens.kt - no per-screen status colours anywhere. AC2: verified live - Room 102 bed grid and the Vacant Beds screen both render VACANT green / OCCUPIED red from the same tokens. AC3: verified live - Unpaid=red, Partial=amber, Paid=green on the invoice list; ACTIVE=green and VACATED=neutral on the tenant directory after checking Ramesh out. AC4: green is pulled to teal and amber to orange for red-green CVD separation, and every state also carries an icon + text label (see LODGY-62). AC5: LodgyTheme provides DarkStatusColors; re-checked the bed grid and invoice list in Dark and the RAG pairs stay correct and legible. Observation for the PO, not a fail: NotesTimelineScreen.kt:47-51 still hardcodes three note-TYPE dot colours as fixed hex that do not adapt to dark mode. Note type is a category, not a RAG status, so it is outside this ticket's ACs - flagging in case you want a follow-up.
